uncited: This method selects a significantly coarser voxel grid resolution (lower $\lambda$) for very large triangle models to minimize grid rebuild time, accepting increased ray traversal overhead to achieve better aggregate frame rates.

It differs from the standard [Grid Resolution Selection via Lambda](3270-grid-resolution-selection-via-lambda.md) approach, which targets moderate scenes with $\lambda \approx 5$, by prioritizing build speed over traversal efficiency for models exceeding several million triangles.
The method modifies the grid resolution parameter $\lambda$ based on the triangle count of the scene.
It does not alter the grid construction algorithm itself but changes the input parameter to the [Grid Resolution Selection via Lambda](3270-grid-resolution-selection-via-lambda.md) method.
- Scene bounding box (used by the parent lambda selection method).
- Grid resolution parameters ($\lambda_x, \lambda_y, \lambda_z$) passed to the grid builder.
Determine if the model is "significantly large" (typically $> 1$ million triangles).
If the model is moderate-sized, use the default $\lambda \approx 5$ as determined by [Grid Resolution Selection via Lambda](3270-grid-resolution-selection-via-lambda.md).
If the model is very large, set $\lambda = 1$ for all dimensions.
Construct the grid using the selected $\lambda$.
- For models between moderate and very large sizes, the trade-off between rebuild time and render time must be evaluated.
- **Time Complexity:** Grid rebuild time decreases significantly with lower $\lambda$.
- **Memory Complexity:** Coarser grids use less memory, though specific memory savings are not quantified in the sources.
This maintains interactivity for large models where finer grids would cause excessive rebuild latency.
It addresses the scalability issues of grid-based ray tracing when applied to models with millions of triangles, where the cost of building a fine grid outweighs the benefits of faster ray traversal.
